clue.text: Bird may take grass as a table delicacy ?

definitions.text: Bird may take grass as a table delicacy ?

parts.words: Bird may take grass as a table delicacy
parts.note: old country speech called asparagus '...-grass', so a small bird's name plus 'grass' gives a vegetable served at table

explanation.surface: A bird helps itself to some grass, treating it as a special dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the folk name 'sparrow-grass' for asparagus: the bird whose name, joined to 'grass', makes a table delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The common house finch-like garden bird is the one whose name forms the folk word for asparagus.

clue.text: Leathery mutton

parts.note: two pictures share one word: a rider's leather seat and a butcher's joint cut from the back of a sheep

explanation.definitionFit: A rider's seat is made of leather, and a joint of mutton from both loins carries the same name.

clue.text: What's the point of Bottom being translated back age one?

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream, Bottom the weaver is 'translated' (transformed) into a donkey, an ass

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word age from its end to its start

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what purpose Shakespeare's Bottom serves when turned into another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AGE into EGA. 'translated' is Quince's own word in the play for Bottom's change into an ass, not a language shift.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender Southern African spear, so it is the thing that delivers the point.

clue.text: Stone sounds to be red basic unit of life

indicators.note: sounds tells us the answer is said like the words that follow, not spelt like them

parts.note: a ruby is red, and the cell is the basic unit of life, so together these say 'ruby cell'

explanation.surface: A gem is said to be a red building block of living things.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'ruby cell' gives the name of a gemstone spelt quite differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubicelle is a yellow or orange variety of spinel, a gem mineral.

clue.text: Peg under the lash ?

parts.note: pictures a wooden toy with a metal peg at its foot, kept spinning by being lashed with a little whip

explanation.definitionFit: This children's toy spins on its tip and is kept going by strokes of a small whip.

clue.text: Old, copper's measurements in legal sessions

parts.note: the as was an old Roman copper coin
sizes are measurements, as of clothing

explanation.surface: An old policeman's vital statistics come up in the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but with 'Old' it is the Roman copper coin AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Assizes were periodic county court sittings in England and Wales, abolished in 1971.

clue.text: Dined on one "hot from hell "

explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to have eaten; and Mark Antony in Julius Caesar pictures the Greek goddess of ruin 'with Ate by his side come hot from hell'.

clue.text: Tackle by the neck

explanation.definitionFit: To scrag is to grab or tackle roughly round the throat; and the scrag is the bony neck end of mutton.

clue.text: Current size Mab adjusted

indicators.note: adjusted says the letters of size and Mab are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Queen Mab, the fairy, tweaks the present size of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' shuffles SIZE and MAB. 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present, but it is the noun: a flow of water, here a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zambesi is a major African river, and a river is a flowing stream of water.

clue.text: Refrain not from refrain here

parts.note: plays the verb 'refrain' (hold back) against the noun 'refrain' (chorus): at this gathering nobody holds back from belting out choruses

explanation.definitionFit: An informal get-together for communal singing is where everyone joins in the choruses.

clue.text: Be ungracious when so strangely glib in cubic form

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the cube word

parts.note: a die is a small cube

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of so and glib are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone is rude when they speak in an oddly glib way, perhaps in a cube shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cubic form' is a small dice cube; 'strangely' shuffles the two short words and 'in' places the result between its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To disoblige is to refuse someone a favour or act against their wishes, the opposite of being accommodating.

clue.text: Fifteen-a siders show some stomach

parts.note: rugby union is played fifteen a side, abbreviated RU
the players on a side are its men

explanation.surface: Rugby players show off a bit of a belly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifteen-a-side is rugby union (RU); its players are MEN. The scan prints 'Fifteen-a-siders' as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumen is the first chamber of a cow's or sheep's four-part stomach, so it is part of one.

clue.text: It's reasonable for an officer astride one horse to retreat

indicators.note: to retreat means to go backwards, so the whole built word is read from the end
astride means the officer's letters straddle the ones that follow, sitting on each side of them

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
one is the Roman numeral I
a horse is a gee-gee in nursery talk, abbreviated G

explanation.surface: A soldier mounts a horse and rides it in retreat, which seems sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: COL 'astride' I and G makes CIGOL, and 'to retreat' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, the quality of what is reasonable.

clue.text: Trees children can't climb

parts.note: the trees here are family trees, charts of ancestry, not wooden ones

explanation.definitionFit: Recorded lines of ancestry are drawn as branching family trees.

clue.text: " Traffics and" (Kipling)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: the missing word completes the title of a 1904 Kipling story collection

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash for the blank after 'Traffics and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling's 1904 collection of stories is titled 'Traffics and' plus the missing word.

clue.text: Tooth-stopping depot with plenty of gas ?

definitions.text: Tooth-stopping depot with plenty of gas ?

parts.words: Tooth-stopping depot with plenty of gas
parts.note: reads like a dentist's surgery that stops teeth and uses gas, but is a roadside place selling petrol (American 'gas')

explanation.definitionFit: A roadside garage selling fuel to motorists; dental fillings and anaesthetic gas give the false picture.

clue.text: A form of illumination for getting off the bus

parts.note: lighting is a means of illuminating a room

explanation.surface: A lamp of some kind is provided for passengers leaving a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to step down from a vehicle, so stepping off is dismounting.

clue.text: Spit

parts.note: in gardening a spit is a measure of soil: the depth or quantity one shovel blade turns over

explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's spit is the amount of earth one digging blade lifts.

clue.text: Their standards can't be faulted

parts.note: describes people whose demands are so exacting that nothing less than flawless will do

explanation.definitionFit: People who insist on flawlessness set standards that cannot be criticised.

clue.text: Floral type of fib, lass

parts.note: Rosa is the botanical genus of roses, a type of flower
a fib is a lie

explanation.surface: A girl tells a flowery sort of untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosalie is a girl's name, so it stands for a young woman.

clue.text: Poets foot it into the Metro cheerfully

indicators.note: into says the answer sits inside the words that follow it in the clue

explanation.surface: Poets hop cheerfully onto the underground train.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'meTRO CHEErfully'. 'foot' looks like a verb (foot it = walk) but is the metrical unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochee is a metrical unit of one stressed then one unstressed syllable, used by verse writers.

clue.text: They are agitated to be getting fat

definitions.text: They are agitated to be getting fat

parts.words: They are agitated to be getting fat
parts.note: describes dairy vessels whose cream is shaken until the butterfat separates

explanation.definitionFit: Butter is made by agitating cream in these vessels until the fat gathers.

clue.text: Hades folk cause the deserted village ?

parts.note: Dis is another name for the underworld, or its god
folk means people

explanation.surface: The inhabitants of the underworld leave a village empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Deserted Village' is Oliver Goldsmith's poem about a hamlet emptied of its inhabitants.
explanation.definitionFit: To depopulate a place, emptying it of inhabitants, is what produced Goldsmith's abandoned hamlet.

clue.text: What the uses of this world produced in Hamlet ?

definitions.text: What the uses of this world produced in Hamlet ?

parts.words: What the uses of this world produced in Hamlet
parts.note: recalls Hamlet's lament 'How weary, stale, flat and unprofitable seem to me all the uses of this world'

explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's weariness with the world is a state of listless boredom.

clue.text: Scotch dancer's call for a dubious scotch

explanation.definitionFit: The cry 'hooch!' is shouted in Scottish reels; and the word is slang for cheap or illicit whisky.

clue.text: No elf badly treated as a criminal

indicators.note: badly treated suggests the letters of no elf are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: An elf who was mistreated is regarded as a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone who has committed a serious crime.

clue.text: A national who's even more so than our museum ?

definitions.text: A national who's even more so than our museum ?

parts.words: A national who's even more so than our museum
parts.note: pictures the national museum in London with a comparative ending added, as if one person were more of it than the museum

explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a citizen of the UK looks like the comparative of the museum's adjective.

clue.text: So loud, Innisfree's glade

parts.note: recalls Yeats's 'The Lake Isle of Innisfree'

explanation.definitionFit: In Yeats's poem the glade is loud with the humming of these insects.

clue.text: Shelter for Confederates

explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side is the one away from the wind; and the Confederates of the US Civil War were General Robert E. Lee's side.

clue.text: Seals that make automatic armed Us infantry retreat

indicators.note: retreat means go backwards, so the soldiers and their weapon are read from the end

parts.note: the Sten was a British automatic gun
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Seals cause machine-gun-carrying American troops to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'retreat', turns the gun and the soldiers round together as one string. The page prints 'automatic-armed' with a hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Signets are small seals, often set in a ring, used to stamp documents.
